Milk is on the menu!

The @USDA has announced that schools will continue to serve low-fat 1% flavored milk to students. This update – advocated for by @CongressmanGT and I – ensures that children are drinking nutritious and filling milk at school. 
https://t.co/pbmK3bcVil

This week, we have more welcome news with the announcement that Abbott Nutrition is restarting production of EleCare and other formulas.

Don’t hesitate to reach out to my Norwich office at (860) 886-0139 more information about the shortage.
https://t.co/P7JQMrO0xk

We just passed the #RestoringHope for Mental Health and Well-Being Act – which funds crucial services and removes barriers to treatment for opioid addiction.

The mental health and addiction crises are felt across eastern Connecticut. This bill bolsters the support many rely on.

ICYMI: This month, the House voted on final passage of the Honoring Our PACT Act – a bill to help ensure toxic-exposed veterans receive treatment for illnesses they developed later in life.

Read more here: https://t.co/AHthEKJmYE

Last week, I visited Perception Programs’ Mobile MAT Van – a treatment van for substance abuse and overdose recovery.

With the use of a federal grant, the van operates in towns across eastern CT, including Putnam, Willimantic, Norwich, and Jewett City. https://t.co/QIIxX2ElsM

I’ll work with anyone who’s serious about getting things done for eastern Connecticut.

This year, @CongressmanGT and I teamed up to introduce the School Milk Nutrition Act—a bipartisan bill to give a boost to dairy farmers and get kids nutritious milk options in school lunches. https://t.co/HMuemD5yxk

Substance use and mental health disorders are rising rapidly, and insurance companies are illegally denying claims for treatment of these conditions. 

Last week, we passed my bill to bolster enforcement of laws that protect coverage for mental & behavioral health conditions. ⬇️ https://t.co/dBPR4I9n9i

As a 2023 Community Project, Somers will receive funding to improve operations at their 40-year-old wastewater treatment plant – cutting pollution in the Scantic River and making the plant way more efficient. https://t.co/c7skbm2FRV

Bringing federal resources to eastern CT to help us fight back against the addiction crisis is one of my top priorities. 

We recently secured a big win in that effort – $915,000 in Community Project funding for SCADD’s residential treatment facility in Lebanon. Watch here ⬇️ https://t.co/FCc5PujMgP

Ending the addiction crisis is going to take collaborative efforts.

Last week, I visited the Overdose Action Team – a joint effort by the City of New London, Alliance for Living, and Ledge Light Health District to lower overdoses in the city through prevention and treatment. https://t.co/rPywp1uy8W

Substance use disorder treatment centers are vital to the health of our communities, but many in eastern CT are facing capacity issues. This week, I visited the new Ridge Recovery Center in Willimantic. It’s opening soon and will be a fantastic facility option for those in need. https://t.co/2Ow4sc46qA

@chairmang @RepTrentKelly @RepJenKiggans ✅ The committee just passed my amendment with @RepAustinScott which requires the Department of Defense to take steps toward establishing a program for the treatment & rehabilitation of Ukrainian soldiers wounded during Russia's illegal invasion.

Very excited to join Hartford HealthCare for the grand opening of the newly renovated Ridge Recovery Center in Windham. 

This spectacular, over 50 bed facility will fill an urgent need for local, high-quality substance use disorder treatment services in eastern Connecticut. https://t.co/DCUHZJ0W9O

At nearly 50 years old, the Stony Brook Interceptor needs to be rehabilitated for continued safe operations at Suffield's Wastewater Treatment Plant. 

It's a costly project for the town, so as a 2024 Community Project, I secured $960k in federal funds to make it possible. https://t.co/v5xkMqpC31

The dialogue came on the heels of China’s extremely aggressive military exercise surrounding Taiwan, reaffirming the critical need for the United States and its allies and partners to come together to ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific through security agreements like AUKUS.

The partisan budget bill will not only cut Medicaid by $800 billion but now we know from the non-partisan budget office that it will trigger an automatic $500 billion cut to MEDICARE. 

This bill is gutting Americans’ health care to pay for a tax-cut for the ultra-wealthy.

Instead of working together to lower costs, the House GOP just jammed through a hyper-partisan budget bill overnight which attacks Medicaid, Medicare, & food assistance in order to extend tax breaks for the ultra wealthy. The net result: the largest deficit increase in history.

There’s a better bipartisan way forward. Balance the tax system so the top 1% and top .01% pay their fair share, reduce the national debt, and strengthen health care and food programs so Americans who are struggling with the high cost of living can get by.

Standing room only at my town hall in Madison last night. Thank you to everyone who joined. 

People are seriously concerned about the 10-year partisan budget bill and its cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, and the ACA. The fight is not over in Congress. There's a better path forward. https://t.co/UjvHscQg4n

At my town halls in eastern CT, people are seriously concerned about health care cuts in the so-called "One Big Beautiful Bill" H.R. 1. These cuts would take away health care for 15 million Americans & put our hospitals in dire financial straits. No wonder hospitals from all across the country are strongly opposed to this bill.

The cuts to Medicaid in the misnamed "One Big Beautiful Bill" are getting WORSE in the Senate version of the bill. I visited Lawrence + Memorial hospital in New London to hear how these cuts will impact services. 40% of L+M patients are covered by Medicaid.

As the American Hospital Association stated, these cuts will take health coverage away from millions nationwide and "strain emergency departments as they become the family doctor to millions of newly uninsured people... the proposal will force hospitals to reconsider services or potentially close." It's not fear mongering. L+M and hospitals all across the country are dumbfounded at these cuts. H.R. 1 needs to be stopped.

All sorts of ugly provisions are slithering out of the “Big Beautiful Bill” – including health care cuts that are so bad, hospitals will be forced to close. 

The House passed the bill in the DEAD OF NIGHT last month. Now, the Senate is making it even WORSE. We've got to block this ugly bill.

This week, I met with the Connecticut Nurses Association, who earnestly stressed how much health care providers rely on strong federal Medicaid funding. As they bluntly stated, Medicaid pays for nurses. We must stop the massive Medicaid cuts in the misnamed “Big Beautiful Bill”. https://t.co/3JafAdGvOB

The health care cuts in the "Big Beautiful Bill" are so massive that hospitals across Connecticut will be forced to scale back services for all patients.

I heard that from L+M Hospital in New London on the shoreline and now from Johnson Memorial Hospital in Stafford near the Massachusetts border. The story is the same – tens of thousands will lose their health coverage and we all will pay. This is the wrong direction for our country. We have to stop this bill.

The Senate just passed a 900-page megabill that will kick millions off their health care and force the hospitals we all rely on to close. 

All to pay for a permanent tax break for the top 1% AND still blow up the deficit by TRILLIONS. 

The fight now moves to the House to stop this bill. I will join the vast majority of Americans who detest this measure and vote NO.

President Trump promised that he would “love and cherish” Medicaid and Medicare. 

Now, he just signed into law the largest cut to Medicaid in U.S. history in a bill that is so fiscally irresponsible, it will also trigger a $500 billion cut to Medicare. All to give the rich a tax break. 

A flagrant violation of the American people’s trust.
